Methods for allocation results

Source: R/08-spax_run.R
spax_allocation-methods.Rd

What to do with the result of spax(), spax_huff() or spax_clm(). These methods read the saved fit or evaluation. A fit does not solve the model again, and an output that was not computed is evaluated when asked for and not stored. A fit in which no start converged has no estimates: coef() gives NULL and the other methods that need outputs stop with "no fit was selected; see summary(x)"; summary(), print() and as.data.frame(type = "starts") still show the starts.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'spax_allocation'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_allocation'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.spax_allocation'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_allocation'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_allocation'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_allocation'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  type = c("parameters", "facilities", "origins", "flows", "starts"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'spax_allocation'
predict(
  object,
  travel,
  demand = NULL,
  outputs = c("allocation", "outside_share"),
  ...
)

Arguments

...

Further arguments: for predict(), those of predict_allocation() (for instance missing_travel); otherwise unused.

object, x

A spax_allocation, or for print() of the summary, a summary.spax_allocation.

row.names, optional

Standard as.data.frame() arguments.

type

The table to return (see above).

travel

For predict(): the requested-origin-by-facility travel matrix, distance of predict_allocation(), in the travel unit of the data.

demand

For predict(): optional demand of the requested origins.

outputs

For predict(): the outputs to return, "allocation" and "outside_share" by default; see predict_allocation() for the others.

Value

print() returns its argument invisibly. summary() returns a summary.spax_allocation. coef() returns a named numeric vector (or NULL), fitted() a numeric vector or matrix, as.data.frame() a data frame and predict() the ae_clm_prediction of predict_allocation().

Details

  • print() shows the specification, the data, the parameters and, for a fit, the selected start, the outside counts used (if any) and the default search.

  • summary() returns a summary.spax_allocation with the specification lines (spec), the parameters table (parameters), the fit summary of fit_allocation() (fit, NULL when evaluated) and the mode; its print method shows them, with the per-start table for a fit.

  • coef() returns the free parameters, fitted or given. Held values are in x$held. In evaluate mode, where every parameter has a value, coef() returns only the decay sigma (or the sigma of each group), the parameter the evaluation takes as free; the other numbers (v0, beta, kappa) are listed as held in as.data.frame(x, type = "parameters").

  • fitted() returns the modelled counts for the observations of a fit (as fitted.ae_multistart_fit() does), and the modelled facility utilization, named by facility, for an evaluation. For a fit with outside counts (see obs_flows()) this is the full target, including the modelled outside count as the column, element or row "(outside)".

  • as.data.frame() returns one of the tables below.

  • predict() predicts requested origins from the saved fit or evaluation with predict_allocation(). Models with demand groups are refused, as there.

Tables of as.data.frame():

typerows and columns
"parameters"parameter, value, status: the free parameters ("fitted" or "given"), then the held values ("held")
"facilities"the facilities of the data: facility_id, supply, attractiveness, utilization, and observed for a fit to facility totals (the sum over groups for totals by group, NA when a group is unobserved); the "(outside)" entry of a fit with outside counts is not a facility and is left out
"origins"the active origins: origin_id, demand, access (the share of demand that goes to a facility of the data), outside_share (pooled over the groups), and for a flow fit with outside counts outside_observed (NA where unknown) and outside_modelled (demand times the outside share)
"flows"the origin-facility cells with modelled flow or observed count above 0: origin_id, facility_id, flow (demand times allocation), and observed for a fit to flows (NA where unobserved)
"starts"the table of starts of the fit (seconds is the time each took)

See also

spax()

Other allocation interface: decay_gaussian(), obs_flows(), prep_data(), spax(), spax_access_values-methods, spax_huff(), spec_clm()
